answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly to duplicate: agents must hold stake or past work that a fresh puppet cannot fake. Before an agent's quill touches the ledger, its messages are hashed and signed with a cipher tied to its stake-weighted key, so flooding the network means burning real collateral on every fake identity. Peers then compare behavioral fingerprints; if fifty accounts echo the same voting pattern from one host, the panel flags the cluster and slashes all of them together, making mass sybils strictly unprofitable.
